title: markup is written as a literal whose segments are trusted and whose holes escape
scope:
how a `Core\Html\Markup` is *written* in expression position, and why the terminal carrier
gets no matching form. It does not touch what the HTML sink escapes with, which is
[0024 § 5](0024.md)'s and *Revisiting*'s.
dependsOnText:
[0024](0024.md) for the sink and the carrier, [0133](0133.md) for the predicate that
made `escape` answer one.
validatedBy:
goal `markup-literal`'s acceptance list, which is where this record's *Verification*
becomes checks.

summary.headline: HTML is written as a backtick literal whose holes are escaped
summary.body:
`` html`

hello {$name}

` `` builds a `Core\Html\Markup` value. The parts you typed are trusted because you wrote them, and every `{$…}` hole is escaped before it is spliced in, which is the same rule the `` template tag already follows. Backticks delimit it because HTML is full of double quotes. `Core\Html::join` composes a list of them. There is no way to turn computed text into markup through this literal, and the terminal output type gets no such literal at all.
